summary: Unexpected routing to variant with KV cache disabled leading to cold-KV misses and p99 spikes
description:
Issue summary:
Customer Nimbus Analytics began seeing sudden p99 latency regressions and 504s for production endpoints between 09:12-09:40 PDT on 2026-03-12. Traffic was routed to a slower variant which exhibited repeated cold KV cache misses and long container init times.

Impact:
- Multiple endpoints for rw-instruct-v1 showed p50 ~60ms (normal) and p99 increased from ~220ms to ~3.1s.
- Customer reported degraded UX and rate of 504s rose to ~2.3% of requests in the window.
- Affected traffic: dedicated capacity pool for Nimbus (reserved rack).

Environment:
- prod-us-west (us-west-2)
- Dedicated capacity pool: nimbus-dedicated-01
- Model pinned at rw-instruct-v1-2026-02-28 for the customer's route

Steps to reproduce (as replicated by Support):
1) Send 1000 concurrent short inference requests (seq len 64) to the customer's public route during routing policy that prefers latency-optimized variants.
2) Observe router decisions in trace; a subset of traffic is routed to variant latency-opt-v2-2026-03-10.
3) Inspect serving logs for that replica set and KV cache metrics.

Observed behavior:
- The variant latency-opt-v2 had KV cache hit rate ~3% for prefixes that should be warm (expected >80%).
- Replica init times for the variant show container pull + init scripts taking 10–25s repeatedly for new workers.
- Router fallback logic chose latency-opt-v2 due to an automated capacity policy when warm replicas fell below threshold. latency-opt-v2 is tagged as latency-optimized in catalog but its runtime config had kv_cache_enabled=false due to a rollout automation bug.

Expected behavior:
- Routing should prefer variants with KV cache enabled and warmed replicas. KV cold misses should not occur for steady-state dedicated traffic.

Logs / dashboards referenced:
- Trace: slack #support thread (see link in comments)
- Serving trace sample: https://observability.redwood/internal/traces/7f4c9f
- KV metrics dashboard: https://observability.redwood/dashboards/kv-cache-nimbus
comments: 2026-03-12 09:30 - Priya Singh: Customer reported p99 spikes and intermittent 504s. Collecting traces and top-of-rack metrics.

2026-03-12 09:42 - Tom Bauer: Initial investigation shows routing to latency-opt-v2 which has kv_cache_enabled=false in its runtime manifest. Possible rollout automation misconfiguration. Escalating to infra eng (#infra).

2026-03-12 10:05 - Mateo Rivera (SRE): Confirmed repeated image pulls for latency-opt-v2; base image size changed in last build causing slow starts. Also saw eviction churn on a subset of GPU nodes in the dedicated pool.
2026-03-12 10:28 - Tom Bauer: Temporarily pinned routing policy to avoid latency-opt-v2 for Nimbus routes. Reduced 504s to ~0.1%. Preparing hotfix to re-enable KV cache for the variant.
investigation_notes:
Findings so far:
- Router's variant selection uses a mix of policy (latency preference) + capacity signals. When warm replica count dipped due to node churn, router sent traffic to latency-opt-v2.
- latency-opt-v2's release on 2026-03-10 contained a manifest change that omitted kv_cache_enabled=true (automation removed the flag). That change slipped past validation because unit tests didn't cover runtime manifest drift.
- The variant also started using a newer base image (2026-03-09) which is ~450MB larger; combined with node network congestion this caused repeated image pulls and long container init times.
- Combined effect: requests routed to this variant suffer cold KV misses plus slow process start -> head-of-line latency and 504s.
- Evidence: KV miss heatmaps, replica start logs, router decision traces attached.

Hypotheses considered and rejected:
- No evidence of model checkpoint corruption. Model files are consistent across variants.
- Autoscaler misconfiguration alone doesn't explain KV flag being off; it's a separate manifest drift issue.
resolution:
Workaround and fixes applied:
1) Immediate mitigation: pinned Nimbus routing rule to exclude latency-opt-v2 at 10:32 PDT; traffic routed back to warmed latency-opt-v1 variants. Customer saw p99 drop back toward baseline within 5 minutes.
2) Hotfix: re-enabled kv_cache_enabled=true in latency-opt-v2 manifest and pushed a controlled canary to one rack (PR referenced).
3) Image rollback: rolled back base image to previous smaller build for latency-opt-v2 to avoid long image pulls.
4) Long-term actions:
   - Add manifest validation check to CI to ensure kv_cache_enabled is present for variants that claim to be latency-optimized.
   - Add router policy change: prefer variants with kv_cache_enabled=true when evaluating latency preference for dedicated pools.
   - Postmortem scheduled and assigned to Mateo Rivera and Elena Novak; runbook updates planned.

Follow-ups / pending items:
- INT ticket created to audit recent automation that mutates runtime manifests (INT-4412).
- QA to run targeted warmup/e2e tests on variant rollout (owner: Platform QA).
- Customer-facing postmortem and SLA credit review requested by CS.
next_steps:
- Complete postmortem by 2026-03-17 and attach to this ticket.
- Deploy CI manifest validator before next variant rollout.
- Monitor KV hit rates and p99 for Nimbus routes for 72 hours post-fix.
resolution_status: Partial mitigation applied; awaiting postmortem and CI fixes
